Description:
Uniting two boxes that touch over a whole face, in six arrangements that differ only in HOW the two
contact faces relate to each other. Everything is axis aligned, so every expected volume is an exact
integer and no triangulation noise enters.

The three that used to fail all have a contact face that is EXACTLY CONGRUENT - same plane, same
rectangle, nothing sticking out on either side:
  same      two 10-cubes stacked, meeting in the full 10x10 square at z = 10
  sameLow   the same, but the upper box is only 5 high - so the SOLIDS differ while the contact face
            is still congruent. This is what rules out "identical bodies" as the trigger.
  sideX     two 10-cubes side by side, meeting at x = 10 - so it is not a peculiarity of the z axis.

The three controls have a contact face that is not congruent, and they always worked:
  partial   the upper box is shifted by 5 in x, so the two faces overlap only in half of their area
  inside    the upper box is 6x6 and sits inside the 10x10 face
  shrink    the upper box is 10 x 9.999 instead of 10 x 10 - one ten-thousandth narrower, and that is
            already enough to take the other path
shrink is the entry that carries the case. It differs from same by 1e-4 in a single edge length, so a
difference in behaviour between the two cannot be a tolerance - it is exact congruence or nothing.

Only the union is tested here. Difference and intersection on a contact of this kind are covered by
TouchingCoincidentFaces, which is about the orientation of the touching faces rather than their extent.
Expected:
Every result is ONE solid, and every volume is exact:
  sameUnion     1000 + 1000     = 2000     a 10 x 10 x 20 box,  6 faces
  sameLowUnion  1000 + 500      = 1500     a 10 x 10 x 15 box,  6 faces
  sideXUnion    1000 + 1000     = 2000     a 20 x 10 x 10 box,  6 faces
  partialUnion  1000 + 1000     = 2000     not a box,          10 faces
  insideUnion   1000 + 6*6*4    = 1144     a box with a step,  11 faces
  shrinkUnion   1000 + 10*9.999*10 = 1999.9  a box with a 0.001 step,  8 faces
The bodies only touch, they never overlap, so in every one of the six the volume is simply the sum of
the two operands.

The FACE COUNT is the sharper half of the check for the first three. Six faces means the contact face
has disappeared from the boundary completely and the result really is a single box - not two shells
stuck together with an internal wall left in them. If sameUnion ever comes back with more than 6 faces,
or as two solids, that is the defect returning.
Status:
OK since 2026-08-28.

Written after the union of two boxes with a congruent contact face started returning TWO solids instead
of one - 1000 and 1000, unmerged. It was found through TouchingCoincidentFaces, whose case a is the
same arrangement, but that file runs 29 calls before reaching it; this one gets there in three.

The cause was a missing Math.Abs on the volume in the final check of the union: the shell that comes out
of a congruent-face contact had its volume with the opposite sign, so the check took it for empty and
discarded the merge. The same slip made pAB in HemisphereOnCylinderThreeWays come back empty, where the
two operands are the same point set and therefore ALL face pairs are congruent - two symptoms that
looked unrelated until the sign was found.

The six arrangements were what narrowed it down, and they are kept for that reason rather than for
coverage: sameLow rules out identical bodies, sideX rules out an axis playing a role, and shrink shows
that one ten-thousandth of an edge length decides which path is taken - so it is exact congruence, not
a tolerance.
